architecture.mechanism: Real-time multi-sensor data fusion (gas, ultrasonic, visual) for autonomous early defect detection to avert catastrophic failure.
architecture.intervention: Retrofit the traction battery pack with an onboard multi-modal monitoring module — per-module gas sensors (H2/CO/CO2 to catch cell venting), acoustic/ultrasonic emission sensors, and thermal imaging — feeding a real-time fusion controller that supervises every DC fast-charge session and derates or aborts charging the instant precursor signatures of thermal runaway appear, replacing the recall's blanket Level-3 restriction with condition-based charging.
architecture.expected_effect: Continuous charge-session health supervision addresses the recall's underlying thermal-runaway hazard at its precursor stage, so DC fast charging can be safely re-enabled for 300+ mile trips while abnormal cells are isolated before failure.
architecture.falsification_test: Run instrumented packs at Level-3 rates with seeded faults (abused/overcharged cells, blocked vents, simulated internal shorts) and measure whether the fusion controller detects and aborts charge before runaway onset; quantify detection latency, false-negative rate, and false-trip rate against a control fleet — any false negative or latency exceeding time-to-runaway falsifies the mechanism.
